clearly_in.why: A run of four one-line flag accessors is stamped out twice, in order: HasFlags, HasPersistentFlags, HasLocalFlags, HasInheritedFlags, then the same four again as HasAvailable*. Each body forwards to the same receiver with HasFlags swapped for HasAvailableFlags, and each carries the matching doc comment. One accessor repeated would be Go; four in the same order with one systematic rename is a copy.
clearly_in.verified: diff of command.go:1796-1813 against command.go:1817-1836 at the pinned sha: every difference is the token `Available` inserted into a method name, a doc comment, or the forwarded call. The statement sequence is identical.

clearly_in.why: MarkFlagRequired/MarkPersistentFlagRequired and MarkFlagDirname/MarkPersistentFlagDirname are the same two-method block written twice: same receiver, same signature, same single-line body forwarding to c.Flags() and then c.PersistentFlags(), same doc-comment structure. Only the operation name changes.
clearly_in.verified: diff of shell_completions.go:24-33 against shell_completions.go:83-92 at the pinned sha: the differences are Required vs Dirname in the method names and forwarded calls, and the reworded doc comments. Both bodies are `return MarkFlagX(c.Flags(), name)` and `return MarkFlagX(c.PersistentFlags(), name)`.

clearly_in.why: HasHelpSubCommands and HasAvailableSubCommands are one function written twice: the same range over c.commands, the same single if-return-true, the same trailing return false, and the same comment placement. Only the predicate called on the sub-command differs.
clearly_in.verified: diff of command.go:1643-1653 against command.go:1657-1669 at the pinned sha: the differences are the method name, IsAdditionalHelpTopicCommand vs IsAvailableCommand, and the wording of the two comments. The control flow is identical statement for statement.
